concepts.title: Mapping the Earth: Latitudes and Longitudes

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Mapping the Earth: Latitudes and Longitudes' refers to.
questions.a: The globe is gridded by imaginary lines - latitudes circling the earth parallel to the equator, including the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, and longitudes running pole to pole - so any place on earth can be fixed precisely at the crossing of its latitude and longitude.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mapping the Earth: Latitudes and Longitudes'.
questions.a: Latitude fixes north-south position, longitude east-west; together they pin any location.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Mapping the Earth: Latitudes and Longitudes' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: hees201.txt lines 53-180 (complexity of mapping the earth, tropics))

concepts.title: The Blue Planet: Oceans and Their Depths

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Blue Planet: Oceans and Their Depths' refers to.
questions.a: Water dominates the earth - the blue planet - with oceans covering most of the surface; the deepest known point lies in the Mariana Trench, and seas like the Bay of Bengal along with straits such as Malacca shape trade, climate and marine life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Blue Planet: Oceans and Their Depths'.
questions.a: Ocean depths like the Mariana Trench dwarf land heights; oceans steer climate and trade.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Blue Planet: Oceans and Their Depths' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: hees201.txt lines 106-352 (blue of the blue planet, Mariana Trench, Bay of Bengal, Malacca))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Continents: Variety on Land' refers to.
questions.a: Seven continents - Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia - carry every kind of landform, from the Great Barrier Reef's tropical seas near Australia to Antarctica's icy wastes, each continent with its own relief, climate and life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Continents: Variety on Land'.
questions.a: Seven continents, endlessly varied: mountains, plains, deserts and ice caps share the land.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Continents: Variety on Land' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: hees201.txt lines 353-430 (the continents: variety on land), 257-268 (Great Barrier Reef))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India in the World Geography' refers to.
questions.a: Sitting between the Indian Ocean and the Himalaya, India touches the world's sea lanes and land routes; the Bay of Bengal on its east and the Arabian Sea on its west tie India to monsoon winds and to the trade geography of Asia, Africa and beyond.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India in the World Geography'.
questions.a: India's location makes it a monsoon land and a crossroads of ocean trade.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India in the World Geography' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: hees201.txt lines 300-352 (Bay of Bengal), India's position in the world picture)
